newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sanwa Bank says ex-manager embezzled 550 mln yen.
newsitem.headline: Sanwa Bank says ex-manager embezzled 550 mln yen.

text.p: Sanwa Bank Ltd said on Thursday that a former branch manager had embezzled 550 million yen and that the bank would file a complaint against him for breach of trust.
The bank fired the manager, who ran a branch in Tokyo's Ota ward, on Wednesday, a Sanwa official told a news conference.

The bank had been conducting an in-house investigation on the alleged embezzlement since early April, when it received a request from a customer to check a deposit made on March 31, the Sanwa official said.
The bank found out that the former branch manager was told by a third party, which the bank official did not identify, to withdraw money from the customer's account, he said.

The former branch manager took the 550 million yen and gave it to the third party, the Sanwa official said. The manager had borrowed heavily due to failed investments, and those loans had been guaranteed by the third party, the official said.
Since the bank believed that people other than its employees had been involved in the alleged embezzlement, it asked the police to investigate in early April, he said.
It also reported the incident to Japan's financial authorities in early April, he said.

Sanwa's managing director Takayo Mochizuki also told a news conference that the bank had paid back 550 million yen to the customer. "Now we will try to recover as much as possible (of the money) ... unless we can, it will become the loss of the bank," he said.

The former branch manager had loans outstanding worth about 100 million yen and had invested in commodity futures and stocks, but the manager did not use any of the 550 million yen he had embezzled to pay back his borrowings, Mochizuki said. Sanwa's share price was unchanged at 1,910 yen at midday on Thursday.
